Kuvitus: talvinen piha. Vasemmalla pulkk: Illustration: a winter yard. On the left a sled stands still and has sunk deep into the snow. On the right a child pulls an identical sled by a rope slanting upwards, and the track it leaves in the snow is shallower.
Kaksi kuvaa samasta tilanteesta. Vasemma: Two pictures of the same situation. On the left the situation diagram: a box is pulled along the floor by a rope that rises obliquely, and above the box a thin blue arrow shows the velocity to the right. On the right the free-body diagram: only the box, drawn as a rectangle, and the forces acting on it as red arrows. The weight G points straight down from the centre, the normal force N from the floor points straight up from the bottom surface and is shorter than the weight, the tension T of the rope starts from the attachment point obliquely up and to the right, and the friction force from the floor starts from the back corner of the bottom surface and points to the left. The velocity is not drawn in the free-body diagram.
Kappaleeseen vaikuttaa voima F, joka läh: A force F acts on an object. It starts from the upper right corner of the object obliquely up and to the right at an angle alpha to the horizontal. The components drawn with dashed lines start from the same corner: the horizontal F x along the x-axis and the vertical F y along the y-axis. The components and the force form a right triangle whose hypotenuse is F. Labels: F x is F times cosine alpha and F y is F times sine alpha.
Free-body diagram of the sled, drawn as a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre, the normal force N from the snow points up from the bottom surface and is shorter than the weight, the tension T of the rope points from the upper front corner obliquely up and to the right at an angle of 35 degrees with its components dashed, and the friction force from the snow points to the left from the back corner of the bottom surface. In the corner are the axes: x to the right, in the direction of motion, and y up.
Opiskelijan piirtämä voimakuvio lattiall: A free-body diagram drawn by a student for a box sliding on the floor, the box drawn as a rectangle. From the centre an arrow G points down, and from the bottom surface an equally long arrow N points up. From the back corner of the bottom surface the arrow of the friction force points to the left, and from the right side of the box an arrow F points to the right. The arrow F is longer than the arrow of the friction force.
Hissikori ja siinä seisova ihminen sekä: An elevator car with a person standing in it, and the person's free-body diagram with the person as a rectangle: the weight G down from the centre and the normal force N from the floor up from the bottom surface. The arrow N is longer than the arrow G.

An elevator car with a person standing in it, and the person's free-body diagram with the person as a rectangle: the weight G down from the centre and the normal force N from the floor up from the bottom surface. The arrows N and G are equally long.

An elevator car with a person standing in it, and the person's free-body diagram with the person as a rectangle: the weight G down from the centre and the normal force N from the floor up from the bottom surface. The arrow N is longer than G, and in addition a red arrow v points up from the side of the object.

An elevator car with a person standing in it, and the person's free-body diagram with the person as a rectangle: the weight G down from the centre and the normal force N from the floor up from the bottom surface. The arrow N is shorter than the arrow G.
Mallikuvio: laatikko liukuu lattialla ta: Model diagram: a box slides on the floor at constant velocity while it is pushed from the handle obliquely downward. The diagram contains only the box, as a rectangle. From the centre the weight G points down. From the bottom surface the normal force N from the floor points up, and it is longer than the weight. The force F of the handle points obliquely down and forward and ends at the upper back corner of the box, where the handle is attached. From the back corner of the bottom surface the friction force points backward, as long as the horizontal component of the force F.
Mallikuvio: pulkka liukuu lumella tasais: Model diagram: a sled slides on snow at constant velocity while it is pulled by a rope at an angle of 30 degrees. The sled is a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre, the normal force N from the snow points up from the bottom surface and is shorter than the weight, the tension T of the rope points from the upper front corner obliquely up and forward, and the friction force from the snow points backward from the back corner of the bottom surface, as long as the horizontal component of the tension, which is drawn with a dashed line.
Mallikuvio: ihminen hississä, joka liikk: Model diagram: a person in an elevator that moves upward and slows down. On the left, as the situation diagram, the elevator car and the person. In the middle the person's free-body diagram with the person as a rectangle: the weight G down from the centre and the normal force N from the floor up from the bottom surface, shorter than the weight. On the right, separately, thin arrows: the blue velocity v up and the orange acceleration a down. They are not forces.
Voimakuvio ruudukolla, yksi ruutu vastaa: Free-body diagram on a grid, one square corresponds to 10 newtons. The object is a square two squares wide and two squares high, and four forces act on it, starting from the middles of its sides: F1 to the right, four squares long, F2 to the left, two and a half squares long, F3 up, three squares long, and F4 down, three squares long.
Neljä tilannetta. Kussakin on vasemmalla: Four situations. Each has a small situation picture on the left and the free-body diagram of the object on the right, in which the object is a rectangle and no surfaces are drawn. Top left: a box rests on a horizontal floor, with the weight G straight down from the centre and an equally long normal force N up from the bottom surface. Top right: a box is at rest on an inclined slope; in the free-body diagram the rectangle is tilted like the slope, with the weight G straight down, the normal force N perpendicular to the bottom surface and the friction force up along the slope from the upper corner of the bottom surface. Bottom left: a lamp hangs from a cord, with the weight G down and the tension T of the cord up from the top surface. Bottom right: a helium balloon is pressed against the ceiling and is at rest: buoyancy up from the centre, the weight down from the centre and the normal force N from the ceiling, which presses the top surface downward, away from the ceiling surface. The buoyancy arrow is as long as the weight and normal force arrows together.
